def-indexed-geometric-site-set:
## Definition

Throughout this page, $\mathbb R$ is a commutative field with $1>0$, a total order compatible with addition and multiplication, and the least-upper-bound property. Let $\mathbb D=\{m2^e:m,e\in\mathbb Z\}$ be its dyadic subfield. For $d\in\{2,3\}$, a nonempty finite indexed site list is a finite list
$$S=((\iota_1,p_1,w_1),\ldots,(\iota_N,p_N,w_N)),$$
where every $\iota_i\in\mathbb Z$ is a distinct stable identifier, every $p_i\in\mathbb D^d$, and each optional weight $w_i$ is either absent (meaning $0$) or belongs to $\mathbb D$. In unweighted mode, a duplicate means equal coordinates; collapse each such class to its least identifier. In weighted mode, a duplicate means an equal coordinate-weight pair; collapse only equal pairs to the least identifier. Equal coordinates with unequal weights remain distinct weighted sites.

The unweighted deduplicated set keeps, for each coordinate value $p$, the entry with least identifier among entries at $p$, and records each discarded identifier in a duplicate map. The weighted deduplicated set keeps the least identifier for each exact pair $(p,w)$ and records only repeated pairs in its duplicate map. A weighted computation retains different weights at the same coordinate; their power values are compared by the ordinary power-distance rule, so a dominated weight may be hidden.

For a finite point set $P\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, its convex hull is the set of all finite convex combinations of points of $P$. Its affine dimension is the dimension of its affine hull. A tuple $p_0,\ldots,p_d$ is affinely independent when the vectors $p_1-p_0,\ldots,p_d-p_0$ form a basis of $\mathbb R^d$; here a basis means every vector has a unique linear expansion in those vectors. This convention makes nondegenerate simplex coordinates unique.
lem-complete-ordered-field-is-archimedea:
## Statement

Let $F$ be a Dedekind-complete ordered field with $1_F>0$. For every $x\in F$, some canonical integer $n\cdot1_F$ satisfies $x<n\cdot1_F$.
lem-linear-cardinal-interpolant-on-an-ed:
## Statement

Let $F$ be a field, let $a,b\in F$ with $a\ne b$, and let $y_0,y_1\in F$. The unique polynomial $P\in F[X]$ of degree at most one with $P(a)=y_0$ and $P(b)=y_1$ is
$$P(X)=y_0+(y_1-y_0)\frac{X-a}{b-a}.$$
def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break:
## Definition

Take a fixed finite universe $U$ of indexed sites as in [[def-indexed-geometric-site-set]], dimension $d\in\{2,3\}$, and an ordered tuple of $d+2$ sites from $U$ with distinct identifiers. A computation using auxiliary sites, such as a planar supertriangle, includes those sites in $U$ from the start and assigns them distinct deterministic integer identifiers. Require that the first $d+1$ sites are affinely independent. Put $h_i=\|p_i\|^2-w_i$, with absent weights interpreted as $0$. Rank all identifiers of $U$ in increasing order, starting at rank $0$, and define
$$P(\varepsilon)=\det\bigl((p_i,h_i+\varepsilon^{2^{r_i}},1)\bigr)_{i=0}^{d+1}.$$
Regard $\varepsilon$ as a positive formal infinitesimal in the rational-function field $\mathbb R(\varepsilon)$, ordered so a nonzero polynomial has the sign of its coefficient at its least nonzero exponent. Expand this finite polynomial exactly and return the sign of its coefficient at the least exponent with nonzero coefficient. If the base is degenerate, return status degenerate-base. The same universe $U$ and ranks are used for every predicate tuple. The procedure never chooses or evaluates a numerical $\varepsilon$; its returned sign is the declared stable-id tie convention for the raw lifted determinant in [[def-certified-geometric-predicate-determinants]].
lem-lifted-power-sphere-determinant-iden:
## Statement

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, let $p_0,\ldots,p_d,q\in\mathbb D^d$, and let their dyadic weights be $w_0,\ldots,w_d,w_q$ (zero when absent). Assume $p_0,\ldots,p_d$ are affinely independent. If $c\in\mathbb R^d$ and $R\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$$\|p_i-c\|^2-w_i=R\qquad(0\le i\le d),$$
define the power difference
$$\Delta(q)=\|q-c\|^2-w_q-R.$$
Let $O_d$ be the determinant of the rows $(p_i,1)$ for $i=0,\ldots,d$, and let $P_d$ be the determinant of the $d+2$ rows $(p_i,\|p_i\|^2-w_i,1)$, including the query row $(q,\|q\|^2-w_q,1)$. Then
$$P_d=-O_d\Delta(q),\qquad O_dP_d=-O_d^2\Delta(q).$$
Thus the sign of $O_dP_d$ is positive, zero or negative exactly when $q$ is respectively inside, on or outside the power sphere. When all weights are zero, this is the ordinary circumsphere convention.
lem-voronoi-vertex-empty-circle:
## Statement

Let $P\subset\mathbb R^2$ be finite and nonempty, and define $V(p)=\{x:\|x-p\|^2\le\|x-q\|^2\ \text{for all }q\in P\}$. If $x$ belongs to at least three distinct cells, then all sites whose cells contain $x$ lie on one circle centered at $x$, no site lies strictly inside that circle, and their convex hull is a polygon with those sites as its vertices.
def-planar-delaunay-voronoi-structures:
## Definition

Use the unweighted deduplicated coordinate set of [[def-indexed-geometric-site-set]]. If its affine dimension is zero, its output is its single site. If its affine dimension is one, sort by the first varying coordinate (use $x$ if it varies, otherwise $y$) and take the chain joining consecutive sites; this is the lower-dimensional output and contains no triangles.

For affine dimension two, a **triangulation of the sites** is a finite family of nondegenerate closed triangles whose vertices are sites, whose union is the convex hull, and whose pairwise intersections are common faces. Its 1-skeleton is the graph with these sites as vertices and all triangle sides as edges; it is connected. The bounded faces of this plane graph are exactly the chosen triangles, and its one unbounded face is the exterior of the convex hull. The boundary edges of the convex hull are subdivided at every site on that boundary. A triangle is **weakly empty-circle** when no site lies strictly inside its circumdisk; other sites may lie on its boundary.

For each site $p$, its closed **Voronoi cell** is
$$V(p)=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:\|x-p\|^2\le\|x-q\|^2\text{ for every site }q\}.$$
A tie belongs to every minimizing cell. The **Delaunay graph** has one vertex for each site and an edge $pq$ exactly when $V(p)\cap V(q)$ contains a nontrivial line segment. A **Voronoi vertex** is a point belonging to at least three distinct cells. It is dual to the convex polygon of the nearest sites; [[lem-voronoi-vertex-empty-circle]] proves that those sites are vertices on one empty circle centered at that point. A **Delaunay triangulation** is a triangulation refining these polygonal Delaunay faces and having weakly empty circumdisks. In a cocircular face the triangulation need not be unique; the chosen algorithmic refinement is the fixed-universe convention of [[def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break]].

The convex-hull boundary is the boundary of the union of the triangles. An unbounded Voronoi cell corresponds to a site on that boundary. No minimum-angle or other mesh-quality condition is part of these definitions.
def-three-dimensional-delaunay-and-weigh:
## Definition

For a weighted site $(p,w)$, define its power distance from $x\in\mathbb R^3$ by
$$\pi_{(p,w)}(x)=\|x-p\|^2-w.$$
Its lifted point is $\widehat p=(p,\|p\|^2-w)\in\mathbb R^4$. A lower face of the lifted convex hull is a face supported by a nonvertical hyperplane $z=\ell(x)$ with every lifted site on or above that hyperplane. The projection of the union of lower faces is the **regular subdivision** of the projected sites; a simplex in that subdivision has an empty power sphere, meaning its common power distance is no larger than that of any input site.

The lex-refined lift is interpreted over the ordered rational-function field of [[def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break]], using one fixed finite universe of all input sites. When every weight is zero, the regular subdivision is the ordinary 3D Delaunay subdivision and power spheres are circumspheres. A weight configuration can hide a site: a weighted site is **hidden** if its lift is not a vertex of any lower face. A nonsimplicial lower face is refined with the same fixed-universe lexicographic lift convention. For projected affine dimension below three, the algorithm reports `lower-dimensional` with that dimension and the exact deduplicated site list, and makes no tetrahedralization claim. A tetrahedral output is claimed only on the full-dimensional branch with nondegenerate projected bases.
thm-lexicographic-lift-tie-break-consist:
## Statement

Fix one finite universe $U$ of uniquely indexed dyadic sites and weights and a dimension $d\in\{2,3\}$. For an ordered tuple of $d+2$ distinct sites whose first $d+1$ sites are affinely independent, the lexicographic lift procedure in [[def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break]] is the determinant sign of one common formal lifted configuration. Every exact nonzero power determinant retains its original sign, every exact zero has a nonzero polynomial tie determinant, and all tuples therefore receive mutually coherent signs. No numeric perturbation parameter is selected or assumed.
def-barycentric-point-location-interpola:
## Definition

Let $T$ be a nondegenerate triangle with ordered vertices $p_0,p_1,p_2\in\mathbb D^2$. For $x\in\mathbb R^2$, its **barycentric coordinates** are the unique scalars $\lambda_0,\lambda_1,\lambda_2$ satisfying $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$ and $x=\sum_i\lambda_i p_i$. They are exact for dyadic $x$: they are obtained by solving the invertible $2\times2$ system with columns $p_1-p_0,p_2-p_0$. The point is in $T$ exactly when all $\lambda_i\ge0$.

Given vertex data $f_0,f_1,f_2\in\mathbb R$, the **barycentric affine interpolant** on $T$ is $I_Tf(x)=\sum_i\lambda_i f_i$. A point-location result is a containing triangle of the triangulation, with a shared-edge or shared-vertex result allowed when the point lies on a face; outside the convex hull its status is `outside-hull` and no containing triangle is returned.

For a finite unweighted site set $P$, the **nearest-site query** returns a site minimizing $\|x-p\|^2$, breaking ties by the least stable identifier. Its hull status is `inside-hull` for $x\in\operatorname{conv}P$ and `outside-hull` otherwise. The minimizer is returned in either case.
lem-euler-count-for-planar-triangulation:
## Statement

For a finite triangulation of the convex hull of $n$ distinct planar sites of affine dimension two, let $k$ be the number of sites on the hull boundary, $E$ the number of edges, and $T$ the number of bounded triangular faces. Then
$$3T=2E-k,\qquad n-E+T=1,$$
and consequently $T=2n-2-k$ and $E=3n-3-k$.
lem-large-delaunay-supertriangle-exists:
## Statement

For every finite full-dimensional dyadic planar site set, a dyadic supertriangle can be chosen to contain every input site strictly and to have all three vertices strictly outside every circumcircle through a noncollinear input triple. If the input has no three collinear and no four cocircular sites, the supertriangle can additionally be chosen so the augmented set has no three collinear sites and no four cocircular sites.
lem-lifted-flip-potential-decreases:
## Statement

Let $ABCD$ be a strictly convex planar quadrilateral in counterclockwise boundary order. Lift its four sites using the common formal heights of [[def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break]]. Let $g_{AC}$ and $g_{BD}$ be the piecewise-affine interpolants on the two diagonal triangulations. Define each interpolant's integral over the quadrilateral as the sum over its two triangles of triangle area times the average of the three vertex heights. If the lifted point $D$ lies strictly below the affine plane through the lifts of $A,B,C$ (the illegal-incircle sign by the coefficientwise determinant identity), then
$$\int_{ABCD}g_{BD}<\int_{ABCD}g_{AC}$$
in the lexicographic order of the formal lift field.
lem-lower-lifted-facets-cover-the-convex:
## Statement

Let $d\in\{2,3\}$ and let $P$ be a finite indexed weighted site set of affine dimension $d$ in $\mathbb R^d$. Lift each site to height $h_i=\|p_i\|^2-w_i+\varepsilon^{2^{r_i}}$ in the fixed ordered formal field of [[def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break]]. A **lower simplex** is the projection of $d+1$ affinely independent lifted sites whose graph hyperplane has every lifted site on or above it. Then the lower simplices cover $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and intersect in common faces. Each lower simplex has a weakly empty power sphere for the original unperturbed weighted sites.
lem-simplicial-four-polytope-facet-count:
## Statement

Let $Q$ be a full-dimensional convex polytope in $\mathbb R^4$ with $m\ge5$ vertices. A facet is a three-dimensional face, and a vertex is an extreme point. Then the number $f_3$ of facets satisfies
$$f_3\le \frac{m(m-3)}2.$$
thm-barycentric-interpolation-and-neares:
## Statement

On every nondegenerate triangle, a point lies in the triangle if and only if its unique barycentric coordinates are all nonnegative; these coordinates also give the unique affine interpolant matching the three vertex data. Interpolants on adjacent triangles with common vertex data agree on their shared face. On an edge, the interpolant is the degree-one cardinal polynomial interpolant. For every nonempty finite site set, the nearest-site query returns a minimizer, breaks ties by least identifier, and reports correctly whether the query is inside or outside the convex hull.
thm-planar-triangle-and-edge-count:
## Statement

For a triangulation of the convex hull of $n$ distinct planar sites with affine dimension two, let $k$ be the number of sites on the hull boundary, $T$ the number of triangles, and $E$ the number of edges. Then
$$T=2n-2-k,\qquad E=3n-3-k.$$
In particular $T<2n$ and $E<3n$.
alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-fli:
## Definition

Input is a finite indexed planar list of exact dyadic sites. Collapse equal coordinates to the least stable identifier. If the affine dimension is zero, return the single site; if it is one, sort by the first varying coordinate (use $x$ if it varies, otherwise $y$) and return the consecutive chain. These branches return no triangles.

For affine dimension two, choose the dyadic supertriangle from [[lem-large-delaunay-supertriangle-exists]]. Add its three synthetic unweighted vertices to one fixed universe $U$; assign their identifiers deterministically below the least input identifier, so the universe and lexicographic ranks are fixed for the whole run. Initialize the triangulation to the supertriangle. Insert distinct input sites in any prescribed permutation.

Locate each new site using exact orientation predicates. In a face interior, replace its triangle by the three triangles joining the site to the face edges. On an interior edge, replace its two adjacent triangles by the four triangles joining the site to the two edge endpoints and the two opposite vertices. Then call `LEGALIZE(p,uv)` on each new edge $uv$ opposite the inserted site $p$ in its incident new triangles. The procedure tests whether $p$ lies inside the circumcircle of the adjacent triangle $uvw$ by the exact orientation-normalized incircle predicate with the fixed height tie-break of [[def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break]]. If illegal, flip $uv$ to $pw$ across the convex quadrilateral and recursively call `LEGALIZE(p,uw)` and `LEGALIZE(p,wv)`. Boundary edges have no adjacent triangle and are legal. Stop when the recursive calls find no illegal edge. After all insertions, delete triangles incident to synthetic vertices and return the remaining triangles and their edges.

The exact raw predicate and its tie-break are separate: [[alg-certified-dyadic-geometric-predicate]] returns exact raw signs including zero; a zero nondegenerate-base sphere test is resolved by the common formal height perturbation in this algorithm. A degenerate base is reported as `degenerate-base` and is not flipped.
alg-incremental-three-dimensional-regula:
## Definition

Input is a finite indexed list of dyadic sites in $\mathbb R^3$, each with an optional dyadic weight. Collapse only exact duplicate coordinate-weight pairs, retaining the least identifier. If the projected set has affine dimension less than three, return `lower-dimensional`, that dimension, and the exact deduplicated list; do not assert tetrahedra.

For affine dimension three, fix the finite lexicographic universe before insertion. Process sites in stable-id order (any stated permutation is allowed if it is fixed before processing). At each prefix, enumerate every four-site subset. If its projected base is affinely dependent, record that tuple with status `degenerate-base` and omit it from tetrahedral candidates. Otherwise solve the unique affine height plane through its four lifted sites. Retain the tetrahedron exactly when every other lifted site in that prefix lies on or above this plane in the ordered formal field of [[def-lexicographic-lift-tie-break]].

After adding a site, delete old tetrahedra whose plane the new lift violates, retain old tetrahedra still supporting, and add every newly supporting tetrahedron containing the inserted site. This finite set difference is the **cavity repair**; no geometric connectivity or running-time bound is asserted. After the final prefix, report the retained lower tetrahedra, the finite `degenerate-base` tuple list, and every weighted site absent from the lower tetrahedra as `hidden`.

For ordinary orientation use [[alg-certified-dyadic-geometric-predicate]]. For weighted lower tests, form the exact dyadic matrix with lifted column $\|p\|^2-w$ and evaluate the finite formal perturbation coefficients using exact integer determinant signs from [[alg-exact-dyadic-determinant-sign]]. The raw exact predicate keeps zero; the formal lift is applied only by this algorithm's declared tie convention.
alg-randomized-history-dag-point-locatio:
## Definition

Assume a finite full-dimensional planar site set in general position: no three input sites are collinear and no four are cocircular. Choose the augmented dyadic supertriangle using the general-position clause of [[lem-large-delaunay-supertriangle-exists]], so the full augmented set has no three collinear sites and no four cocircular sites. Fix the common tie ranks before processing.

Draw one permutation uniformly from all $n!$ permutations of the distinct input sites and insert in that order using [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]]. Maintain a directed acyclic graph (DAG) whose leaves correspond one-to-one with current triangulation triangles. Initially it has one leaf for the supertriangle. When a face is split into three triangles, turn its leaf into an internal node with pointers to the three new leaves. When an edge split replaces two triangles by four, each old leaf points to the new leaves whose interiors meet its old triangle. When a flip replaces two triangles by two, each old leaf points to both new leaves. A leaf that is later replaced is treated in the same way; cross-pointers keep each current leaf linked to its triangle.

To locate the next site, start at the root and test the query against the children of the current node using exact orientation predicates. Descend to the child triangle containing the query and continue until reaching a current leaf. Under the augmented general-position condition the query lies in a unique triangle at every stage. Each internal node has at most three children. After construction, remove synthetic-vertex triangles for the returned Delaunay triangulation; the history DAG is the insertion-time point-location structure.
thm-incremental-planar-delaunay-correctn:
## Statement

For every nonempty finite indexed dyadic planar site set, after duplicate collapse the algorithm of [[alg-incremental-planar-delaunay-edge-flips]] terminates. In the affine-dimension-two branch, after each insertion the augmented triangles are exactly the $d=2$ lower simplices of the common fixed-universe formal lift, as defined in [[lem-lower-lifted-facets-cover-the-convex-hull]]. After removing synthetic vertices, the output triangulates the input convex hull with weakly empty original circumdisks and coherent lexicographic ties. In dimensions zero and one, the algorithm returns the defined single site or consecutive chain.
thm-three-dimensional-lower-hull-coverag:
## Statement

For a finite dyadic weighted site set of projected affine dimension three, the algorithm of [[alg-incremental-three-dimensional-regular-cavity-repair]] terminates. Its output tetrahedra cover the convex hull, meet in common faces, and have empty power spheres in the original weak sense. In the zero-weight case they are ordinary Delaunay tetrahedra. A site is hidden in the fixed formal lower hull if and only if it is omitted from every output tetrahedron. The algorithm reports every coplanar four-site base as `degenerate-base` and makes no tetrahedralization claim on the lower-dimensional branch.
thm-randomized-history-dag-expected-loca:
## Statement

For a full-dimensional planar input in general position, augmented by a fixed supertriangle so the full set is also in general position, a uniform random permutation, the local insertion updates, and history DAG of [[alg-randomized-history-dag-point-location]] give expected $O(n\log n)$ total point-location work in the exact-predicate-call model. Triangle creation and DAG storage have expected $O(n)$ size. A conservative worst-case bound for all location walks is $O(n^3)$; no randomized expected bound is asserted for nonuniform or adversarial insertion orders.
thm-three-dimensional-delaunay-output-si:
## Statement

For $n\ge4$ weighted sites of projected affine dimension three, the number of 3D Delaunay tetrahedra or weighted regular tetrahedra returned by the fixed formal lift is at most $n(n-3)/2$, hence $O(n^2)$. No planar $O(n)$ bound or mesh-quality guarantee is asserted.
ex-cocircular-four-site-lexicographic-ti:
## Statement

For the square sites $A=(0,0),B=(1,0),C=(1,1),D=(0,1)$ with identifiers $1,2,3,4$ and zero weights, the unperturbed lifts are coplanar. In the four-site universe the perturbation $h_i=\|p_i\|^2+\varepsilon^{2^{r_i}}$ selects diagonal $BD$. Adding three synthetic identifiers below these four sites multiplies all four perturbation exponents by $8$, so the algorithm's augmented universe selects the same diagonal. Both selected triangles are weakly empty in the original, unperturbed sense.
ex-collinear-sites-lower-dimensional-out:
## Statement

For unweighted sites with distinct ids at $(0,0),(1,0),(1,0),(2,0)$, duplicate collapse retains the least id at $(1,0)$, and the affine-dimension-one output is the ordered two-edge chain from $(0,0)$ to $(2,0)$.
ex-scattered-linear-interpolation-over-d:
## Statement

On the Delaunay triangle with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(0,2)$ and vertex data $0,2,2$, the query $(1/2,1/2)$ has barycentric weights $1/2,1/4,1/4$ and affine interpolated value $1$.
